newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.2 pct in April -- Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.2 pct in April -- Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.2 percent in the four weeks of fiscal April versus March, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.
The index rose 6.1 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 6.0 percent in the week ended May 3 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
The week's modest improvement was reflected mainly in department store sales, due to improved demand for apparel and accessories, the Redbook Research report said.
"Retailers confirmed that warmer weather throughout the country was supporting sales of seasonal merchandise," it said.
The results in March were a little shy of target, the report said.

"Retailers set more modest targets for April than for March, despite an extra shopping day and, if the trend continues, may adjust their expectations downward again in May to be more in line with current results," it said.
